requirements.note: Newest-first inset-grouped list showing show, title, date · length, and a Played/Unplayed label plus a filled or empty circle. It has a search field and a count line ('420 episodes · 295 unplayed').
An 'Unplayed only' switch in a row filters the list (293 → 292 when one is marked from the filtered list) and the count updates.
Shows tab lists all 12 shows with 'N episodes · M unplayed'; tapping one pushes that show's episodes newest first. Every show has the same purple waveform icon.

Detail screen shows show, title, date · length, summary, and a Play button that marks the episode played and changes to 'Playing' with a Pause button. Add to Up Next and Mark as Played/Unplayed rows sit below.
Leading circle button on each row toggles played/unplayed in place. There are no swipe actions.

The + button on each row adds to Up Next (turns into a check). Up Next reorders by dragging the grip in Edit mode or with Earlier/Later buttons, and Remove works. But the queue is a hand-made stack of rows with text buttons, not a list, and swipe-to-delete does not work.
After a relaunch, played states and the Up Next contents and order (3 items, reordered) were kept.

bugs: A horizontal swipe on an episode row or Up Next row registers as a tap and opens the episode detail, instead of showing swipe actions or doing nothing.
Tapping a row during the dark-mode switch didn't respond at first, then pushed the detail screen later. The Episodes tab was then left sitting on a detail screen without my having opened one.
tells: No swipe actions anywhere: no swipe to mark played or queue on episode rows, and no swipe-to-delete in Up Next.

Up Next is not a table: rows have no separators or cell background, with loose purple 'Mark Unplayed' and red 'Remove' text buttons under each item. In Edit mode it shows custom 'Earlier / Later / Remove' capsule buttons instead of the system delete and reorder controls.
The Up Next large title has a tiny '4 episodes · 198 min' subtitle jammed right under it, which is not a system navigation-bar layout.
Every show uses the same tinted waveform glyph, so there is no artwork to tell shows apart.
Episode rows in a show's list repeat the show name on every row.

At the largest text size the in-row buttons become big grey capsules ('Mark Unplayed', 'In Up Next'), the checkmark overlaps 'In Up Next', and 'Mark Unplayed' sits off-centre with no icon. Up Next's 'Mark Unplayed' / 'Remove' lose their alignment and 'Remove' slides under the tab bar.
The navigation title on a detail screen is the show name rather than the episode, while the show name is repeated again in the card.
A.scroll: The 420-row list scrolls and flings smoothly with no blank or popping rows, and scroll position is kept when switching tabs (about a 19 pt shift). Pull-down and return to the top behave normally.

requirements.note: Newest-first list: a 'Latest release' feature card, then 'Recent episodes (419)' rows with generated show artwork, show, title, date · length, and a Played/Unplayed dot label, plus an 'In Up Next' glyph when queued.
An All episodes / Unplayed segmented control filters the list (featured card plus 291 more = 292 unplayed). The same control appears on each show's page.
Shows tab lists the 12 shows A–Z with artwork, 'N episodes' and 'M unplayed'. Tapping one opens a show page with a header and that show's episodes.

Detail screen has large artwork, a link to the show, title, date · length, played status, summary, and a Play episode button that marks it played, switches to Pause, and shows 'Playing · playback preview' plus a Now Playing bar. A Queued toggle and Mark as unplayed are there too.

From the list: a leading swipe gives a 'Played' action, a trailing full swipe adds to Up Next, the ⋯ button opens a system menu (Play / Mark as played / Add to Up Next), and the featured card has its own Play button.

Up Next uses the system Edit mode with red delete circles, a Delete confirmation and reorder handles; dragging a handle moved item 1 to 3. Swipe left to delete also works, and the tab shows a count badge.
After a relaunch, played states, Up Next items and their order (3 items, reordered) were kept. The playing state resets, which is fine.

tells: Heavily themed: a warm cream background, rust accent, and letter-spaced monospaced section headers ('LATEST RELEASE · NEWEST FIRST', 'P / 05' on the artwork) read as a designed brand look rather than stock iOS.
The Now Playing mini-player is a flat full-width bar above the tab bar, not the system tab-bar accessory, and it disappears on pushed screens.
Rows have both a ⋯ button and a disclosure chevron. In Up Next edit mode they also get the reorder handle, which is crowded and makes the date wrap ('Oct 26, 2026 · / 63 min').
Pinned section headers ('RECENT EPISODES 419 EPISODES', 'ALL EPISODES') float over half-visible row content while scrolling.
The segmented control's labels stay small at the largest text size while everything around them grows (system behaviour, but it stands out).
Extra decorative tagline headers ('A little curiosity goes a long way.', 'Find your familiar voices.', 'A listening list, made by you.') take up screen space.
B.scroll: Smooth throughout: slow drags and flings showed no blank or late-appearing rows, artwork is there immediately, and scroll position was kept when switching tabs. Sticky headers blur over content the way a system list's would.

why: B covers every requirement with real iOS list behaviour: leading and trailing swipe actions, system context menus, the system Edit mode with delete and reorder, swipe-to-delete, a tab badge and a Now Playing bar. It holds up in dark mode and at the largest text size. A works and looks closer to stock iOS on its main screens, but it has no swipe actions, its Up Next is a hand-built stack of rows with text buttons, and sideways swipes are treated as taps that open the episode.
